parsed.summary: The paper introduces ALBIREO, a detector-agnostic, codec-free, adaptive inference framework for video object detection on edge devices. ALBIREO uses a Kalman filter-based uncertainty trigger, a rescue mechanism, and an empty-scene screen to improve the accuracy-energy-latency tradeoff. Evaluated on the BDD100K dataset with three detectors and two Jetson platforms, ALBIREO achieves up to 17.6% energy savings while maintaining AP@50 within ±1.2 percentage points of per-frame inference.

chk_problem.value: Video object detection on edge devices is computationally expensive and energy-intensive due to the need to process long frame streams with high temporal redundancy.
chk_problem.paper_quote: Video object detection on edge devices requires running computationally expensive detectors over long frame streams, leading to high energy consumption and sustained GPU utilization.

chk_method.value: ALBIREO uses a Kalman filter-based uncertainty trigger, a rescue mechanism, and an empty-scene screen to adaptively skip frames and improve efficiency.
chk_method.paper_quote: We present ALBIREO, a detector-agnostic, codec-free, adaptive inference framework that wraps off-the-shelf object detectors and decides when detector invocation can be safely skipped based on scene content and per-object temporal state.

chk_data.value: BDD100K dataset’s multi-object tracking (MOT) validation split with 200 dashcam clips and 7 object classes.
chk_data.paper_quote: We evaluate ALBIREO on the BDD100K dataset’s multi-object tracking (MOT) validation split using three architecturally distinct detectors (YOLO11x, YOLO26x, and RF-DETR-Large) on two NVIDIA Jetson platforms (AGX Thor and AGX Orin).

chk_setup.value: Evaluation on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor and AGX Orin platforms using YOLO11x, YOLO26x, and RF-DETR-Large detectors.
chk_setup.paper_quote: We evaluate ALBIREO on the BDD100K MOT across three architecturally distinct detectors (YOLO11x, YOLO26x, RF-DETR-Large) and two Jetson SoC generations (AGX Thor and AGX Orin).

chk_primary_result.value: ALBIREO improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6% on Thor and 14.4% on Orin.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: On the primary YOLO26x configuration, at its default operating point, ALBIREO improves the accuracy–energy–latency tradeoff over Vanilla per-frame inference: on Thor, it improves AP@50 by +0.8 pp while reducing energy by 17.6%, frame time by 8.8%, and per-frame energy-delay product (EDP) by 24.9%; on Orin, it achieves the same AP@50 gain with 14.4% lower energy and 26.1% lower EDP.

chk_secondary_result.value: ALBIREO forms the upper AP@50–EDP Pareto frontier over evaluated baselines in the target operating region (AP@50 ≥ 0.50).
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: Sweeping the primary uncertainty threshold on YOLO26x traces an AP@50–EDP Pareto frontier that dominates the evaluated frame-skipping baselines (FixedSkip-N, CTD, Statues) within the target operating region (AP@50 ≥ 0.50).

chk_baseline.value: Compared against FixedSkip-N, CTD, Statues, and ERD-only baselines.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: We compare ALBIREO against five families of frame-skipping baselines.

chk_conclusion.value: ALBIREO is a practical drop-in efficiency layer for off-the-shelf edge video detection pipelines, improving the accuracy-energy-latency tradeoff.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: These results show that using the object-level temporal state can serve as a practical drop-in efficiency layer for off-the-shelf edge video detection pipelines.

chk_limitation.value: Kalman dynamics may drift under erratic motion, and the empty-scene screen is domain-dependent.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: The constant-acceleration Kalman dynamics fit many vehicle-dominated dashcam scenes, but can drift under highly erratic motion, such as a pedestrian making an abrupt lateral move at a crosswalk.
